title: Master & Dynamic Partners with Alcantara for new MH40 Over Ear and MH30 On Ear Headphones | audioXpress
snippet: The new gunmetal/black Alcantara editions of the MH40 Over Ear and MH30 On Ear headphones are available at specialty sound and retail stores across North America and are available online for $399 and $329, respectively. [...] These Alcantara edition headphones offer a new take on Master & Dynamic’s existing gunmetal/black color selection and add to the company’s rapidly growing product line. Partnering with Alcantara S.p.A., allowed Master & Dynamic to explore the unique material’s benefits, adding durability and stain resistance to help meet the brand’s commitment to long-term durability. The material covers the headband, ear cups, and ear pads, with the added benefit of keeping the ears warm. [...] The MH30 Alcantara model are foldable supra-aural headphones, using 40mm neodymium drivers (32 ohms) in a lighter (260g) construction, also featuring Premium Alcantara, stainless steel, aluminum and the same two detachable woven cables. The MH30 was designed to be a more mobile “thinking cap” with Alcantara material on headband exterior and interior surfaces, ear pads, and earcup insets. All metals have anodized finish or PVD (physical vapor deposition) coated for superior durability.

title: Master & Dynamic MH30 headphones: Built to last and sound great - CNET
snippet:
9239552.jpg

With the MH30 you get a rugged canvas carry pouch, one cable with an iPhone compatible mic and control, and another plain “straight” cable. The MH30 sports 40mm drivers, and impedance is rated at 32 ohms. This handsome headphone is offered in three color schemes: silver/brown leather, gunmetal (gray)/black leather, and black metal/black leather. The MH30 weighs 9.2 ounces (260 grams). [...] More from CNET

The MH30 is a closed-back, on-ear headphone design, but when I first heard it I thought it was an open-back on-ear. That is, it doesn’t have the crushed, inside-my-skull sound I get with most on-ears. That’s really something. [...] The MH30 won’t light up the ears of listeners craving oodles of high-res detail; it’s not that kind of sound. But if you like big and bold, the MH30 will make every tune a little sweeter and richer than you’ve heard before. Boosted bass may be the current fashion, but what if you’re not into bass?
